entities.name: Stress symptoms
observations: In a large adult multicentre cross-sectional study, medically unexplained symptoms were associated with higher extracellular water, lower intracellular water, and lower phase angle.

Stress-symptom participants had lower morning and higher evening cortisol than lean asymptomatic participants; extracellular water correlated positively with evening cortisol and negatively with morning cortisol.
The study supports association, not causality, and used a specific dual-frequency BIA device.

entities.name: hs-CRP
observations: Higher hs-CRP was associated with lower phase angle and higher extracellular water in the large adult study of stress-related symptoms.
Across a review of human populations, higher CRP was generally associated with lower phase angle, with heterogeneous effect sizes.

entities.name: Cortisol
observations: Higher evening cortisol and lower morning cortisol were associated with altered bioimpedance profiles: higher extracellular water and lower phase angle in adults with stress-related symptoms.

In children/adolescents, serum hs-CRP correlated strongly with hair cortisol, but the available results did not establish a direct cortisol association with phase angle, resistance, reactance, ECW, or ICW.

entities.name: Inflammatory biomarkers
observations: Human studies across general, aging, obesity, chronic kidney disease, COVID-19, ICU/hospitalized, psoriasis, and other populations generally found lower phase angle with higher CRP, TNF-alpha, IL-6, and IL-10.
Associations were heterogeneous in magnitude and may be modified by BMI, hydration, nutrition, disease severity, device, and study design.

entities.name: Stress inflammation bioimpedance association
observations: Human evidence supports an association between stress/inflammatory measures and bioimpedance, most consistently higher extracellular-water distribution and lower phase angle with higher inflammatory burden or chronic-stress symptoms.
Evidence for perceived stress, HRV, leukocyte count, and individual resistance/reactance values is sparse or context-dependent; most studies are observational or cross-sectional.
